statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96222 (GHSA-vrv5-2jg9-4mmr, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vrv5-2jg9-4mmr): KeyInfoX509Data can accept serialized certificate formats with attacker-controlled chain metadata instead of a plain X.509 certificate, contributing to certificate-forgery and token-spoofing paths. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.0 to 8.0.4, fixed in 8.0.5; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 8.0.32 (SDK 8.0.132 and 8.0.426): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/474, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. The dotnet8-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root and FSharp directories), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet8-sdk source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.134-r0, 9 builds, as 8.0.128, 8.0.130 and 8.0.132 were not published for 3.23; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.131-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.2 to 8.0.4 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 sources), inside the affected range; 8.0.133-r0 and every later build carry System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.5 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.33 and later sources), which includes the fix; the fixed assembly is also larger than the previous one. The Roslyn build-task .deps.json still records an older 6.0 reference to the package, but no 6.0 copy of the assembly ships in any build.

CVE-2026-96222 (GHSA-vrv5-2jg9-4mmr): KeyInfoX509Data in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml can accept serialized certificate formats containing attacker-controlled chain metadata instead of requiring a plain X.509 certificate, contributing to certificate-forgery and token-spoofing paths. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.0 to 8.0.4 as affected, fixed in 8.0.5, and shipped the fix in .NET 8.0.32 with SDK 8.0.426: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-vrv5-2jg9-4mmr, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/474, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. We read every published dotnet-sdk-8 build in the DHI Debian repository, 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.428-1 (10 builds, each for amd64 and arm64), after verifying each against its index checksum, recursing into the zip archives they carry, and read the version resources of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll; both architectures match in every build. No debug-symbol packages are published for this source, and the dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. Every build carries System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version> and under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version> in the SDK root, FSharp and dotnet-watch tool directories; 8.0.422-0 and 8.0.423-0 also carry a copy in the dotnet-format tool directory. Each build also has a reference assembly, metadata without implementation used only at compile time, under packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref. In 8.0.423-0 to 8.0.425-1 the implementation copies have file version 8.0.2926.32403 (product version 8.0.29), the assembly shipped in the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.4 NuGet package, except the 8.0.423-0 dotnet-format copy, which is product version 8.0.26; in 8.0.422-0 they are product version 8.0.26, and its dotnet-format copy 8.0.0. All of these are older than the fix. From 8.0.426-0 on, every implementation copy has file version 8.0.3226.50405 (product version 8.0.32), the assembly shipped in the fixed 8.0.5 NuGet package. The range ends at 8.0.426-0, the first published build with the fix.
